record.paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
record.original_question: Are the charge-specific multi-particle correlations observed in heavy-ion collisions genuine Chiral Magnetic signals from QCD chiral anomaly effects in strong magnetic fields, or are they backgrounds produced by local charge conservation modulated by elliptic flow, and can proposed parameter-isolating tests such as isobar-beam collisions deliver a decisive limit or answer?

evidence.quote: QCD chiral symmetry, and its violation by quantum effects ("chiral anomaly"), leads in the presence of strong external magnetic fields to a number of charge specific multi-particle correlations commonly referred to as "Chiral Magnetic".

Unfortunately, not all of the observed systematics (pT, √s, correlation with the EP, ..) follow precisely the prediction, and also making the strongly Lorentz contracted magnetic field decay slowly enough to have any measureable effect at all is nontrivial.

Therefore, the leading background explanation of local charge conservation modulated by elliptic flow remains a very strong contender, even if it has its own problems with some of the observed regularities.
Eventually a future test at RHIC with isobar beams (|B| not equal const, v2 = const) could set a decisive limit if the question has not been settled by then.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions, the QCD chiral anomaly in the presence of a strong, transient electromagnetic field is predicted to induce charge-dependent multi-particle azimuthal correlations, collectively known as the Chiral Magnetic Effect (CME): an electric current along the magnetic field producing a charge separation across the reaction plane. A standard observable is the three-particle correlator γ_{αβ} = ⟨cos(φ_α + φ_β − 2Ψ_RP)⟩, where φ_α, φ_β are the azimuthal angles of charged particles of species α,β ∈ {+,−} and Ψ_RP is the reaction-plane angle, together with related charge-dependent harmonics. A competing, purely conventional explanation attributes the observed signal to local charge conservation (correlated emission of opposite-sign pairs) modulated by elliptic flow v_2.

Setup of the proposed isobar test: collide two nuclei with the same mass number but different atomic numbers (e.g., ⁹⁶₄₄Ru + ⁹⁶₄₄Ru versus ⁹⁶₄₀Zr + ⁹⁶₄₀Zr) at the same √s_{NN} and centrality. Then v_2 (and hence the flow-driven background) is approximately equal between the two systems, while the magnetic-field magnitude |B| differs by a controlled amount. A genuine CME contribution should produce a difference in the charge-dependent correlators (e.g., the ratio of Δγ to v_2) between the two species that scales with the |B|² difference, whereas a purely flow-driven background should not.

Question: Determine whether the charge-dependent multi-particle correlations measured in heavy-ion collisions are dominated by a genuine CME signal arising from the QCD chiral anomaly in strong magnetic fields, or instead by background from local charge conservation modulated by elliptic flow. In particular, decide whether an isobar-collision program of the form above can yield, and does yield, a decisive quantitative limit (or measurement) on the CME fraction of the observed charge-separation signal.
artifact.category_tag: Chiral Magnetic Effect in heavy-ion collisions
artifact.status_search_result: The STAR Collaboration carried out the proposed isobar test (Ru+Ru vs Zr+Zr at √s_NN = 200 GeV) with a pre-registered blind analysis of ~3.8 billion events, published in Phys. Rev. C 105, 014901 (2022). No CME signature satisfying the predefined criteria was observed, providing a strong upper limit on the CME contribution. Subsequent analyses (Phys. Rev. C 106, L051903) accounting for differences in multiplicity and flow between the isobars are consistent with a small finite CME fraction of order (6.8±2.6)% of the observed Δγ. Thus the isobar program has delivered a decisive constraint, but the question of a nonzero residual CME signal remains under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Search for the chiral magnetic effect with isobar collisions at √sNN = 200 GeV by the STAR Collaboration
status_evidence.snippet: No CME signature satisfying the predefined criteria was observed in the blind isobar analysis.
status_evidence.claim: The proposed isobar test was performed and yielded a decisive null result against the predefined CME criteria.

status_evidence.title: Implications of the isobar-run results for the chiral magnetic effect in heavy-ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Once the observed difference in multiplicity and collective flow are quantitatively taken into account, the STAR results could be consistent with a finite CME signal contribution of about (6.8±2.6)%.
status_evidence.claim: After background corrections, a small but nonzero CME contribution remains compatible with the data, leaving residual interpretation open.

status_evidence.title: Experimental Search for the Chiral Magnetic Effect in Relativistic Heavy-Ion Collisions: A Perspective
status_evidence.snippet: A perspective on the experimental search for the CME after the isobar program.
status_evidence.claim: The status remains an active research topic with the isobar program providing the principal current constraint.
